correctness.rationale: For every integer \(k\geq3\), the total leaf-coverage capacity of \(k\) burning rounds is \((k-1)^2+1\). Equality forces the time-labelled cyclic tiling of disjoint pendant intervals; a shorter sequence cannot reach this cap. All tilings burn all vertices, including the last pendant parent core, and their sources meet the standard unburned-before-ignition constraint. Replacing a single source fixes its uncovered leaf interval, forcing all sources except the penultimate core/pendant toggle. Unique cyclic orders give \(2n(k-1)!\) optima and \(n(k-1)!\) components isomorphic to \(K_2\). Independent BFS-based exhaustive C++ checks for \(k=3,4,5\) and constructive Python checks for \(k=3,\ldots,7\) agree. The universal inference is in the proof, not from finite enumeration.

value.rationale: Beyond the known scalar burning number, this solves the natural equality-case optimizer classification at every sharp pendant-capacity boundary, with an exact factorial number of ordered histories and maximally fragmented one-source replacement mobility (a matching). The condition \(n=(k-1)^2+1\) is forced by a sharp leaf-coverage capacity, not an arbitrary slice. The result quantifies adaptability of optimal ignition schedules rather than merely recomputing the scalar invariant.
